_source: Analyst, 04-Aug-2026, on the NextPower supplier bundle: 'if remittance E-mail value is not blank then delivery method value is EMAIL & if remittance fax is not blank but remittance-email is blank then the delivery method is EMAIL, otherwise blank.' Given twice, verbatim, after the generated FBDI shipped Delivery Method empty on every row.
_scope: Client NextPower, the supplier bundle. Registered under 'Supplier' with applies_to_all_sheets, so it reaches Supplier, Supplier Address and Supplier Site — the three objects that carry the column.
_why_a_new_dated_file: The rule was already authored, on 28-Jul and again on 30-Jul, and read correctly. It shipped blank anyway.

The likeliest cause is a regression introduced on 04-Aug: an overlay rule stopped running when the CONVERSION carries its own rule for the same field that is newer. That guard is right in general — it stops the overlay overwriting a rule an analyst typed five minutes ago — but a rule SEEDED onto a conversion carries the date it was seeded, not the date it was decided. supplier_transform_mappings.json seeds a Delivery Method CASE_WHEN off the Email/Fax TRANSACTION FLAGS, and the 28-Jul note says in as many words that it must be retired or 'the two CASE_WHENs will both target this field'. A stale seeded rule reading columns the extract does not have produces exactly what was reported: blank on every row.

Re-dating the instruction is the fix the architecture already has for this. Under one dated store the newest statement wins; this is the newest statement. It beats any rule seeded before today without weakening the guard that protects a rule an analyst has just typed.
_open_question: The analyst's sentence assigns EMAIL in BOTH branches — 'if remittance fax is not blank but remittance-email is blank then the delivery method is EMAIL'. It was stated that way twice. Implemented exactly as written. The 28-Jul version of this rule said FAX there; if that is still intended, change the fax branches back to FAX and re-date.

rules.note: E-mail branches are tested first, so a row carrying both still reads from the e-mail column — which is what 'preference to EMAIL' meant on 28-Jul and is unchanged. Every plausible spelling of each column is listed: a branch on a column the extract does not have reads as blank and falls through, so naming several costs nothing and one wrong guess costs the whole rule. The default is blank, never a guessed code.
